_about: Single source of truth for every rendering, and the auditable term ledger (check 5). ONE rendering per referent for the whole book. Before you romanize any name, check here. status per entry: 'attested' (form used in English scholarship / an established English name), 'provisional' (romanization mine, not found in outside sources; the builder appends a visible marker), 'decided' (a project style call, e.g. standard pinyin of a fictional name). Sections are rendered as glossary headings; keys starting with '_' are ignored.

卫达夫.note: Communist agent ('Old Wei'); watches the market from the street.

易君年.note: Communist ('Old Yi'); Ling Wen's superior; keeps a painting-and-scroll shop.

凌汶.note: Communist; writer, author of the novel Winter; a merchant's widow.

秦传安.note: Communist; a doctor with his own clinic.

田非.note: Communist; library clerk who found the hidden meeting room.

林石.note: Communist; clerk at the Rentai Bank; shot in the leg during the arrest.

梁士超.note: Prisoner; claims to have served in the Nineteenth Route Army.

方云平.note: Communist ('Old Fang'); missed the meeting; the gunman on Pu'enjishi Road.

董慧文.note: Communist; young schoolteacher at Minghui Primary School.

陈千元.note: Communist; a reporter; close to Dong Huiwen.

陈千里.note: Communist operative, the novel's central figure (introduced in a later chapter).

龙冬.note: Ling Wen's late husband, killed in Guangzhou.

浩瀚.note: Working alias ('the vast') of a senior Communist leader the enemy is hunting.

游天啸.note: Captain of the Longhua detective squad; secret man of the Party Affairs Investigation Section.

穆川.note: Director of the garrison's Judge Advocate's office; You Tianxiao's nominal superior.

叶启年.note: You Tianxiao's teacher; deputy director of the Special Operations Headquarters.

姚探长.note: Chinese detective of the Settlement's Central Police Station.

翁副官.note: A Cantonese staff officer about the Garrison Command.

蔡军长.note: The Nineteenth Route Army's general; the historical Cai Tingkai.

宋先生.note: The man arranging Miss Tao's release and marriage; with Mrs. Song (宋太太).

李国杰.note: Grandson of Li Hongzhang; principal of the 1933 China Merchants embezzlement case.

李鸿章.note: Late-Qing statesman, founder of China Merchants; the 'Grand Secretary Li' (李中堂) of the gossip.

陈孚木.note: Go-between in the China Merchants case; fled and was placed under a warrant.

杜月笙.note: Shanghai underworld boss and Nationalist ally; the 'tycoon Du' (杜大亨).

徐枕亚.note: Mandarin-Ducks-and-Butterflies romance novelist; name-dropped by Miss Tao.

金焰.note: Korea-born film star, the 'Emperor of Film'; leads Cuckoo Soul Abroad.

委员长.note: Chiang Kai-shek, in his title as chairman.

工部局.note: Governing body of the foreign-run International Settlement.

巡捕房.note: The Settlement's police (and, by extension, a police station); the Central Station is 中央捕房.

侦缉队.note: The Longhua garrison's plainclothes criminal-investigation squad, under You Tianxiao.

军法处.note: The garrison's military-justice department; its head (处长) is rendered 'Director'.

淞沪警备司令部.note: The Shanghai-Woosung garrison HQ at Longhua; also 龙华警备司令部, 'the Longhua Garrison Command'.

党务调查科.note: Kuomintang political-intelligence organ; forerunner of the wartime Bureau of Investigation and Statistics (中统).

特工总部.note: Insiders' name for the Investigation Section's Nanjing base at the Zhanyuan.

中央组织部.note: The Kuomintang organ over the Investigation Section.

十九路军.note: Cantonese army that fought at Shanghai in 1932, later sent against Communists in Fujian.

斧头帮.note: Shanghai assassins' gang; linked to the killing of the China Merchants director.

招商局.en: the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company
招商局.note: Founded by Li Hongzhang; center of the 1933 embezzlement scandal.

向导.note: The Chinese Communist Party's central organ of the 1920s; Haohan published in it.

南昌行营.note: Chiang Kai-shek's field HQ for the anti-Communist campaigns.

龙华.note: District southwest of Shanghai; seat of the garrison and its prison; site of the 1931 martyrs.

玄武湖.note: Lake against the northeastern wall of Nanjing.

四马路.note: Today Fuzhou Road, in the International Settlement; books, theaters, brothels, and the market.

浙江大戏院.note: Real cinema at 123 Zhejiang Middle Road (Laszlo Hudec, c.1930), by the Fourth Avenue market; the author's named location, NOT the later 大上海大戏院. English form mine.

世界大旅社.note: A named 1930s Shanghai hotel with a roof-garden amusement ground (carousel, skating rink, billiards) overlooking the market; listed among the novel's real settings, and distinct from the Great World (大世界) amusement palace. English form mine.

白云观.note: 'White Cloud Temple'; base of the detective squad in the Chinese city.

同春坊.note: Lane running to the gate of the Gezhi school and Minghui Primary School.

格致公学.note: English-style boys' school run by the Municipal Council; where Tian Fei studied.

苏州河.note: The creek down which the market's produce is boated in.

金利源码头.note: Shanghai wharf; among those mortgaged in the China Merchants case.

报恩塔.note: The ancient Longhua pagoda, beside the garrison compound.

南市.note: The old Chinese city south of the Settlement.

枫林桥.note: Landmark on the road out to Longhua.

老闸捕房.note: Settlement police station; Ling Wen is first held here.

兰心大戏院.note: The Settlement's foreign theater, by its standing English name.

南京路.note: Shanghai's grand commercial street; opposed to grim Longhua.

徐家汇.note: District with the postal sub-office named as the letter's drop.

普恩济世路.note: Shanghai street where Fang Yunping opened fire.

下关.note: Nanjing's riverside district and railway station on the Yangtze.

鸡鸣寺.note: Temple by the Nanjing city wall, passed on the drive.

神策门.note: Gate in the Ming wall of Nanjing.

瞻园.note: Nanjing garden housing the Special Operations Headquarters.

明城墙.note: The great Ming-dynasty wall of Nanjing, along Xuanwu Lake.

骰子.note: The pair of dice: the group's recognition sign, and the thread the enemy has hold of.

牌九.note: Domino gambling game; the cover for the meeting.

阴丹士林.note: Brand of colorfast synthetic dye; the blue of the schoolboys' gowns.

旗袍.note: The fitted dress; Miss Tao's, with the letter in its lining.

危害民国紧急治罪法.en: the Emergency Law for Crimes Endangering the Republic
危害民国紧急治罪法.note: 1931 Nationalist law; carried the death penalty, used against Communists.

西施.note: Legendary beauty of Yue sent to ruin Wu; here the code name of a planted agent.

五卅运动.note: 1925 anti-imperialist upheaval after Settlement police shot demonstrators.

一·二八.note: The 1932 Battle of Shanghai against the Japanese.

大红袍.note: 'Great Red Robe,' the most prized of the Wuyi rock teas.

训政.note: The Nationalist 'tutelage' period of one-party rule.

特务工作之理论与实际.en: The Theory and Practice of Secret-Service Work
特务工作之理论与实际.pinyin: Tewu gongzuo zhi lilun yu shiji
特务工作之理论与实际.note: The scarce secret-service manual Mu Chuan asks You to bring.

冬.note: Ling Wen's novel; Dong Huiwen has read it.

蓝钢快车.note: The overnight express between Shanghai and Nanjing.

青天白日旗.en: the Blue Sky and White Sun flag
青天白日旗.note: The Nationalist emblem flown over the garrison gate.

党国.note: Nationalist formula fusing party and nation.
